newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka army trains its men on the laws of war.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka army trains its men on the laws of war.

text.p: Sri Lanka's army, accused by human rights groups of rights violations against minority Tamils, has started training its officers on the laws of war, the International Committee of the Red Cross said on Tuesday.
The ICRC said in a statement it was conducting a week-long course in Colombo on humanitarian laws of war for 10 army majors and 15 captains.

"This first batch of officers will be sent as teams to all training centres and operational areas to disseminate this knowledge to the Sri Lanka army," the statement quoted Brigadier T.M. Bohoran, commanding officer of the army's 12 Brigade, as telling the participants.

The army, fighting a 13-year-old ethnic war against the separatist Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) guerrillas, has been accused by the rebels and human rights groups of arbitrary arrests, illegal detentions and other rights abuses, including rape and murder.
The LTTE is fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in this predominantly Sinhalese Indian Ocean island's north and east.
The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the war. The LTTE says the number is higher, with the majority of victims being Tamils.
The military says human rights abuses are isolated and committed by rogue soldiers. It says the army is committed to punishing misbehaviour and investigating all reported disappearances.

"Humanitarian values in war should never be seen as impairing military operations or seen as a constraint by having to make unnecessary concessions to the enemy," the ICRC statement quoted Gerard Peytrignet, who is the head of the ICRC's Sri Lankan delegation, as saying.
"On the contrary, the strict application and respect for humanitarian law will always contribute, in the long term, to achieve goals such as winning hearts and minds of people," he said.
